why: An off-by-one in the custom period's check refuses a range of a single day, which the Summary tab must accept.
An import left behind after the code that used it was removed is a mistake only the linter reads for.

find:
if method != "GET" and origin is not None and origin.removeprefix("http://") not in allowed:
            raise ApiError(403, "forbidden_origin", "This server only accepts writes from its own page.")
why: The refusal of a write sent from another site's page is removed, so any page the analyst visits could change the watchlists.
Undoing a review twice answers 404 (not found) instead of 409 (conflict), a wrong status the page would read as the review having vanished.

find: assert str(monday.year) in heading and (trials, changes) == (2, EXPECTED_CHANGES)
replace: assert str(monday.year) in heading and (trials, changes) == (2, changes)
why: A walk's assertion compares the change count with itself, so it checks nothing: the defect E-026 that rule R-005 forbids.
A line in the defect log names a check file that does not exist, so the defect it records has nothing catching it.
The guard against a second press while Mark reviewed is in flight is dropped, so a double click sends two reviews and leaves an Undo that fails (E-033).
Editing the NCT ID no longer clears the failure sentence of the last add, so it stays beside a different ID (E-035).
A refused page number is shown as a registry failure, with a Retry that cannot succeed and an empty form (E-036).
The sidebar is no longer redrawn after a review changes, so its Needs review badges stay stale after Mark reviewed and Undo.
